metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Officially limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Goedert has missed the last two contests due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, but his return to drills this week puts game action back on the table for the ninth-year tight end. He likely will need to string together consecutive days of on-field work to give the Eagles peace of mind and clear him to play Sunday versus the Jaguars in London. For the time being, though, Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins are the healthy TE options on the active roster, and the team can still use one more elevation on Zach Ertz to reinforce the position

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: Dallas Goedert returned to practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Goedert has missed a couple of weeks with a knee injury. He could have a chance to return this weekend if he can continue to practice.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Back at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) is practicing Wednesday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
metadata.analysis: With Goedert returning to the field after recently being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, this marks his first visible step forward in his recovery from a sprained MCL in his right knee. His participation Wednesday puts the Eagles tight end back on the radar for Week 5, and his practice level and any game designation later in the week will provide more insight about his availability.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert Returns to Practice, Should Play on Sunday
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) is back at practice on Wednesday, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. From what McLane understands, Goedert "should be able to play on Sunday" in the Week 5 clash in London with the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Eagles will see how the week goes before clearing Goedert to return this weekend, but fantasy managers have to be happy with the news. The 31-year-old veteran is recovering from a sprained right MCL in his knee that he suffered in the Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans. Goedert only had one catch for four yards in that game, but he caught four of five targets for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the season-opening win over the division-rival Washington Commanders and could be one of quarterback Jalen Hurts' top targets this weekend if he returns to face the Jaguars. Receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) could miss Sunday's game, and running backs Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen) are both injured. Goedert should be in play as a TE1 in fantasy if he makes his return in Week 5.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) won't play Sunday
metadata.description: Dallas Goedert (knee) won't play in Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
metadata.analysis: As expected, Goedert is going to be sidelined for another game in Week 4 as he continues to recover from a knee issue. Devonta Smith (hamstring) is also going to be sidelined, so the Eagles will need to look to Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon to step up in this matchup against Los Angeles.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Ruled out for Week 4
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams.
metadata.analysis: With Goedert set to miss another game while recovering from the sprained MCL in his right knee and Devonta Smith set to miss with a hamstring injury, Philadelphia will need to lean heavily on Dontayvion Wicks and first-round rookie Makai Lemon to key the passing game. Goedert has yet to practice since suffering his injury in Week 2 against the Titans and remains week-to-week.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert Officially Ruled Out for Week 4
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) has officially been ruled out for his team's Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams, per Zach Berman of The Athletic. Goedert suffered a sprained MCL in Week 2 and was given a multi-week return timeline at the time of the injury, so it's not a surprise that he will return to action in Week 4. The Eagles did not place Goedert on Injured Reserve, which indicates that the team thinks he has a chance to return within four games of the injury. However, Week 4 will be his second straight game on the sidelines, and he's not guaranteed to return in Week 5 either. Philadelphia will also be without star wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) on Sunday, leaving the team down its two top pass-catchers. Eagles wideouts Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon are likely to see increased workloads, and tight end Zach Ertz could be a deep-league streamer option for fantasy managers in Week 4.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Another DNP on Thursday
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) officially didn't practice Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Goedert has yet to practice since emerging from Week 2 with an MCL sprain in his right knee, and Friday's injury report may seal his fate for a second straight game after sitting out Monday's loss at Chicago. During that contest, the breakdown of offensive snaps among the Eagles' active tight ends was Johnny Mundt's 26 (of 50), followed by Zach Ertz's 19 and E.J. Jenkins' 13.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) not at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Dallas Goedert (knee) was not seen at Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: As expected, the veteran tight end was not seen participating in Philadelphia's practice on Thursday. He's still recovering from a knee injury and is likely to miss more time before he's back in the lineup. Zach Ertz will continue to see increased run for however long Goedert remains out moving forward.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Not spotted at Thursday's practice
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) isn't present for the start of practice Thursday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
metadata.analysis: Goedert looks to be on his way to a second consecutive practice absence to kick off Week 4 prep. After sitting out Monday's loss to the Bears due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, Goedert is fighting an uphill battle to return Sunday against the Rams. If Goedert remains sidelined, Zach Ertz would have a chance to step up as the top pass catcher in an Eagles tight end room that was paced in snaps by Johnny Mundt on Monday.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert Does Not Practice on Thursday
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) officially did not practice on Thursday as the team prepares to face the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4. Goedert has now missed back-to-back practices with a sprained MCL that he suffered in Week 2's win over the Tennessee Titans. With Goedert's status remaining uncertain, tight ends Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz, and E.J. Jenkins are all expected to have a role if he misses Sunday's matchup. While Ertz offers the most upside of the group, none of the three are fantasy-relevant options in Week 4. Fantasy managers should continue monitoring Goedert's practice status on Friday, but he appears unlikely to suit up against the Rams.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) not practicing Wednesday
metadata.description: Dallas Goedert did not practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Goedert remains likely to miss another game.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Sits out walkthrough
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) didn't take part in Wednesday's walkthrough.
metadata.analysis: Goedert already has missed one game due to an MCL sprain in his right knee and likely will continue to trend toward absences in future weeks until he returns to the practice field in some capacity. In Monday's loss at Chicago, Johnny Mundt started in place of Goedert and logged 26 of 50 offensive snaps, which was followed by Zach Ertz's 19 and E.J. Jenkins' 13. A similar breakdown of TE reps is likely between the trio until Goedert is back in the lineup.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Won't play Monday
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Goedert was unable to practice all week due to an MCL sprain that he sustained during the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Titans. Zach Ertz was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, and he figures to be elevated to the active roster for Monday's game and provide depth at tight end behind Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins. Goedert's next chance to play is Week 4 against the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 4, though he should be considered week-to-week.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - No practice again Friday
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) didn't practice Friday.
metadata.analysis: Goedert has yet to log any on-field work since emerging from a Week 2 win in Tennessee with an apparent MCL sprain, which typically requires multiple weeks to recover from. The Eagles haven't officially ruled him out for Monday's game at Chicago, but Saturday's injury report should provide clarity on his status for at least Week 3. In Goedert's likely absence, Johnny Mundt, E.J. Jenkins and practice-squad member Zach Ertz will be the candidates to fill in at tight end.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - No practice Thursday
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Goedert didn't return after departing this past Sunday's win in Tennessee due to a knee injury, and Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN reported Monday that the tight end was expected to miss some time due to an MCL sprain. Thus, Goedert's lack of activity Thursday isn't a surprise, but the team has yet to officially rule him out for Monday's contest at Chicago. Assuming Goedert is inactive Week 3, Johnny Mundt, E.J. Jenkins and perhaps newcomer Zach Ertz, who is on the practice squad, will be manning tight end for the Eagles.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) to avoid IR, expected to miss a few weeks
metadata.description: Dallas Goedert (knee) will not be placed on injured reserve but is still expected to be sidelined for a few weeks.
metadata.analysis: Goedert suffered a knee injury last week and the team considered placing him on injured reserve, but they are not going to do so, as he is only expected to miss a few weeks while he recovers. This is good news for fantasy managers of the veteran, but they will still need to find a substitute for him for the foreseeable future while he's out. Zach Ertz will step up and see more work for the Eagles in his absence.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert suffers MCL sprain, to miss a few weeks
metadata.description: Dallas Goedert suffered a sprained MCL in Sunday's win over the Titans.
metadata.analysis: The injury is expected to sideline Goedert for at least a few weeks. DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon should all step up even more in the passing game for Jalen Hurts.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Set to miss time with MCL sprain
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) was diagnosed Monday with a sprained MCL and is expected to miss a few weeks, Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN report.
metadata.analysis: Goedert went down in the second quarter of Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans with the injury and now appears to be headed for a multi-week absence. While Goedert missed the entire second half of the Week 2 win, Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins handled tight-end duties, but neither saw major involvement in the passing game. During Goedert's upcoming absence, wideouts Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon could be the biggest beneficiaries of added targets behind No. 1 receiver DeVonta Smith.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert to Miss a Few Weeks With Sprained MCL
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) suffered a sprained MCL in his knee in the Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday and is expected to miss a few weeks, sources told Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. It is a big blow for the Eagles' offense going forward, as the next two men up on their TE depth chart are Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins. Goedert's injury will most likely mean more targets all around for receivers DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, and rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon. The 31-year-old Goedert had a big game in the Week 1 season-opening victory over the division-rival Washington Commanders, catching four of his five targets for 77 yards and two touchdowns, but he was able to reel in just one pass for four yards on two targets on Sunday against the Titans before his knee injury knocked him out. Because of Goedert's big role in the Eagles' passing game when healthy, fantasy managers should find a way to keep him stashed while he rehabs his MCL sprain.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Set for tests on knee injury
metadata.description: Goedert (knee) is slated to undergo an MRI on Monday after exiting Sunday's 24-20 win over the Titans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Goedert played 19 snaps on offense and recorded a four-year reception on two targets before sustaining the knee injury in the second quarter. Though the Eagles deemed Goedert questionable to return, he never ended up checking back into the game and is now set to undergo further testing as the team looks to determine the severity of his injury. If the knee issue keeps Goedert from suiting up in the Eagles' Week 3 matchup with the Bears next Monday, Johnny Mundt (2-8-0 receiving line, 64 percent snap share Week 2) would be the next man up at tight end.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert Set to Undergo MRI on Monday
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of his injury, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL.com. Rapoport noted that a player undergoing an MRI on their knee typically indicates that they'll miss time, but managers should stay tuned for further updates on his status. The 31-year-old exited during the first half of Sunday's win over the Titans and did not return, finishing Week 2 with just one catch for four yards. Goedert is a major part of the Eagles' offense, and he represents one of Jalen Hurts' most reliable and physical targets after AJ Brown was traded to New England during the offseason. The tight end had 77 yards and two catches during his last fully healthy game in Week 1, so the Eagles and fantasy managers will hope his absence doesn't last too long. Assuming he does miss time, Johnny Mundt would step up as the team's primary tight end.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert held to one catch before knee injury
metadata.description: Dallas Goedert caught one of his two targets for four yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Goedert left the game with a knee injury and did not return. Look for the team to update his status heading into a Week 3 matchup against the Bears. The Eagles are all of a sudden very thin at tight end with Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra both on injured reserve already.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert (ankle) questionable to return
metadata.description: Eagles TE Dallas Goedert (ankle) is officially listed as questionable to return Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Goedert appeared to have suffered the injury blocking in the second quarter. Johnny Mundt will see an increase in snaps with Goedert sidelined.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert - Iffy to return due to knee injury
metadata.description: Goedert is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans due to a knee injury.
metadata.analysis: Goedert reeled in one of two targets for a four-yard gain before leaving the game in the first half after he appeared to get upended while run blocking, per Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer. According to McLane, Goedert checked into the medical tent to be evaluated further, but the Eagles could examine him more thoroughly in the locker room before deciding whether he's able to return to the contest. The Eagles will be left with Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins as their options at tight end if Goedert ends up sitting out for the rest of the game.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert Questionable to Return With Knee Injury
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) is questionable to return against the Tennessee Titans, according to the team. Goedert had one catch for four yards before leaving the game. Johnny Mundt is next up at tight end if Goedert can't return, with E.J. Jenkins also available for Philadelphia.

metadata.title: Dallas Goedert's TE1 Stock Jumps After Big Opener
metadata.description: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert picked up where he left off last season, catching four of five targets for 77 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-22 win over Washington. He led Philadelphia in receiving yards despite Jalen Hurts attempting only 25 passes, and his five targets were second on the team. Goedert scored 11 times in 2025, so another two-touchdown performance immediately makes last year's breakout look a little harder to dismiss as touchdown luck. The 77 yards matter just as much. Goedert topped that mark only twice all of last season, and Philadelphia now has a different-looking target tree after trading A.J. Brown during the offseason. DeVonta Smith remains the top receiving option, but Goedert showed in Week 1 that there is room for him to stay heavily involved. His fantasy stock is clearly higher coming out of the opener, with another top-10 tight end season looking more realistic than it did a week ago.
